title: Reading Date Fields and Weekday Information
learningObjectives: Explain date attributes, weekday values and calendar calculations and its role in Python applications.
Choose appropriate datetime classes and methods for date attributes, weekday values and calendar calculations.
Predict the output of representative PY17.4 operations.
Identify invalid values, formatting ambiguity or timezone risks related to date attributes, weekday values and calendar calculations.
Apply date attributes, weekday values and calendar calculations in a small, deterministic Python program.

understand.concept: Date and datetime objects expose year, month and day fields, while date objects provide weekday methods. `weekday()` numbers Monday as 0 and Sunday as 6; `isoweekday()` numbers Monday as 1 and Sunday as 7. Calendar-aware calculations are clearer when these documented conventions are explicit.
understand.whyItMatters: Scheduling, reports and business rules often depend on weekdays, month boundaries and leap-year behaviour.
understand.analogy: Date-time values are like entries on a calendar plus the hands on a clock; a duration measures the distance between two entries.
understand.analogyLimit: Real calendars include leap years, time zones and daylight-saving transitions that a simple wall calendar analogy does not fully model.
understand.summary: Reading Date Fields and Weekday Information teaches reliable representation and manipulation of Python date-time values.

explain.narrative:
## Read date attributes
Use `.year`, `.month` and `.day` to access calendar components. A datetime object also exposes hour, minute, second and microsecond.

## Weekday numbering
`weekday()` returns Monday=0 through Sunday=6. `isoweekday()` returns Monday=1 through Sunday=7. Remember which convention a downstream API expects.

## Calendar calculations
Use `calendar.monthrange(year, month)` to obtain the first weekday and number of days in a month. Leap-year logic should use calendar APIs rather than handwritten divisibility rules when possible.

## Avoid hard-coded assumptions
Month lengths vary and leap years affect February. Test boundary dates such as the end of a month and year.

examples.title: Read date fields
examples.code:
from datetime import date
day = date(2026, 11, 19)
print(day.year)
print(day.month)
print(day.day)
examples.explanation: Date fields are available as read-only attributes.

examples.title: Get weekday using weekday()
examples.code:
from datetime import date
day = date(2024, 1, 1)
print(day.weekday())

examples.title: Get weekday using ISO numbering
examples.code:
from datetime import date
day = date(2024, 1, 7)
print(day.isoweekday())
examples.explanation: ISO weekday numbering represents Sunday as 7.

examples.title: Count days in a month
examples.code:
import calendar
first_weekday, days = calendar.monthrange(2024, 2)
print(days)

examples.title: Read both date and clock fields
examples.code:
from datetime import datetime
moment = datetime(2025, 8, 9, 16, 20, 5)
print(moment.date())
print(moment.time())
examples.explanation: date() and time() return the corresponding component objects.
